proposal.name: Let the proved cores run recordings

issue_plan.name: Let the proved cores run recordings
issue_plan.summary: Four ordered plumbing changes cover issue #26: media inspection and staged file operations, a durable pieces caller, a durable session caller, and app integration with spool migration. The cores decide recording life, joins, recovery and retention; callers save decisions before acting. The app accepts Start during finishing, remembers Stop during startup, reports each end, retries failed work and removes eligible pieces after three days. Each change updates SPEC.md and README.md, distinguishing tested support from app behavior and recording the Mac checks required before rebuilding the owner's app.

issues.title: Inspect recording fragments and stage files for core-directed publication
issues.body:
Issue #26 moves recording life and pieces to the released session and pieces cores. This first change supplies media inspection and disk operations for their callers, tested independently; it does not switch the app. Use plain Go with no decoder, cgo or network dependency. The app already requires session, pieces and handover v0.1.0. Leave dependencies, proved cores, models, explorers and trusted configuration unchanged.

Add inspection in internal/mp4 and staged operations in internal/spool. Read each piece's length from its own track and fragment metadata in positive integer milliseconds, including sample durations and sizes supplied through defaults. Use 4,000 ms when its bytes supply no usable duration; a short final piece with timing metadata must retain its actual length. Keep duration fallback separate from join readability.

For the new join path, a piece is unreadable if opening or reading it to its end fails, its prefix differs from the recording's opening segment, its boxes do not fill it exactly, or its media data is shorter than its fragment declares. Inspect the entire fragment and media bounds, including sample sizes, offsets and defaults. Support the writer's actual box forms, size widths and timescales without decoding media. Preserve mp4.Read, File and Track behavior used by the self-test.

Provide separate operations to write and flush a piece under its owned hidden name, publish it with a nonreplacing hard link, discard its hidden remnant, prepare a joined file, publish that file without replacement, and discard its partial output. Flush directories when publishing or removing names. The caller supplies piece numbers and ordered inventory; these operations choose neither the next number nor capture finality. After a kill, distinguish an operation's completed publication from a conflicting file. Never overwrite a named piece or joined file.

Join preparation reads every requested closed piece once in order and writes the opening once plus each readable fragment once to a hidden output. An unreadable piece contributes no partial bytes; continue with later pieces and return exact omitted numbers. Preserve fragment timing so the recording jumps over omissions instead of closing them up. Flush the complete hidden output but leave publication to the caller, after it saves the omissions and durations. Output-write failure or no readable piece fails preparation with no named output. Original pieces remain unchanged.

Keep spool.Create, Recording, PutOpening, PutPiece, Pieces and Join signatures and the self-test's core-free PutPiece and Join behavior. Add a separate new path. Preserve internal/spool/spool_test.go's string fixtures and old first-gap/prefix expectations. Read internal/mp4/mp4_test.go's box builders and decode-time, large-box and malformed-header tests before selecting concrete plan files.

Test on Linux with real temporary folders: nonreplacement, interrupted writes, full reads and read errors, truncated boxes and sample data, foreign opening, unreadable middle piece followed by readable media, all unreadable, output failure, exact ordered output and preserved timeline gaps. Use valid hand-built MP4 boxes for targeted cases and the ORIGINAL init.mp4 and piece-000001.mp4 through piece-000006.mp4 described in internal/spool/testdata/writer/README.md for compatibility. Assert all six are readable, their durations come from metadata including the short last piece, and an intact join omits none. These are generated picture and tones from onair selftest -keep at 31952c1, not a captured meeting.

The readable planning snapshot contains that README but no MP4 bytes. Check the authoritative checkout for #30's originals. If absent there too, restoring them from #30 is Merger work for a person; do not fabricate replacements, skip the compatibility test or claim it passed.

Include SPEC.md and README.md in the concrete plan: describe tested support while the app still uses its old recording path. Keep docs/PRD.md's intended behavior. Run captured format, vet, build and test checks. Leave internal/mac and cmd/onair/main_darwin.go untouched.

issues.title: Persist and execute the pieces core's requests
issues.body:
Build on the merged fragment inspection and staged spool operations to add a complete caller for github.com/gitdek/onair/core/pieces/pieces v0.1.0 in internal/spool, separate from legacy PutPiece and Join. Test it directly; app adoption is a later change. The core alone decides numbering, finalization, join/publication requests, retries, hand-over and removal. Call transitions, never explore.go or model bounds. Leave cores, dependencies and trusted configuration unchanged.

Configure 21,600 pieces (24 hours at four-second cuts), cumulative join-interruption limit 3 and millisecond durations. Store pieces.json in each recording directory with core state, stable identity, stable joined-file name and detailed caller errors. Serialize only numbered pieces, including an open one, plus all logical scalar state; restore unused capacity as zero slots. Persist each accepted transition by whole hidden write, flush, rename and directory flush before its effect. Failed saves authorize no further effect. Save enough caller data to reproduce errors after restart.

AcceptPiece precedes a hidden write, with length from the bytes or 4,000 ms. Report durable flush, save, publish only on Name, then report naming and save. Write failures retain their reason, prohibit later pieces from that capture and execute remnant disposal. Reaching 21,600 closed pieces immediately returns a stop reason; no further piece is accepted or overwritten. Finalize only after the host reports permanent capture end and no piece remains open. With no closed piece, finalization produces Empty, never join or hand-over.

Execute Join with every closed piece in core order. Report omissions to ReportJoinPrepared, using the durations already saved, and persist the manifest before publishing the flushed output with a nonreplacing link. Save its target name before preparation and keep it across retries. An all-unreadable or failed join hands over nothing, retains pieces and reports the error and spool path. Never bypass this ordering through legacy Join.

Execute Handover through unchanged internal/delivery Prepare, Load and Run and its existing core, for this same recording and single joined file. Report success once the folder is confirmed to hold it, including recovery of success not yet saved in pieces.json. Explicit delivery failure becomes HandoverFailed. A stopped operation remains an unresolved pieces request and returns its error to the host; do not report it as explicit hand-over failure. Resume the existing delivery and its saved destination, preserving ErrStuck behavior.

Expose loading/reconciliation, piece input, final capture, eligible-work execution, retry requests and retry/stopped status. Restore the whole record and call Recover exactly once per launch with authoritative named-piece and named-join observations; save before effects. Accept named-but-unreported pieces, discard unnamed open remnants before other work, and reuse a named join with its saved manifest. Discard unnamed join output before retry. Three interrupted joins fail on that launch; subsequent launch or person retries retain the count and can succeed. Never repeatedly recover in one process to evade the limit.

Drive AskRetry and ScheduleRetry for failed work. Relaunch retries failed joins and failed/unresolved hand-overs; stopped hand-overs resume their outstanding request. For retention, read handover.json's existing durable handedOver timestamp without changing delivery's implementation or format. Count three full days from that same origin, not a retry or delayed success report; unknown time cannot authorize early removal. Only ReportThreeDaysElapsed and RequestRemoval authorize piece deletion. Persist the request and report completion only when all requested pieces are absent. Failed/interrupted removal resumes later. Delivery retains ownership of joined-copy cleanup.

Honor internal/delivery/delivery_test.go's Failed-versus-Err distinction, folder pinning, conflicts, slow-copy retention origin and kill tests. Test this caller with real temporary folders, a controlled clock and faults before/after each pieces save and disk effect: unnamed/named-but-unreported pieces, saved manifests, named joins, all-unreadable/output failure, three interruptions and successful retry, stopped/failed delivery, delivered-before-reported success, exact 72-hour retention, delayed reports, clock rollback and interrupted/failed removal. Undelivered pieces never disappear; at most one whole joined file reaches the archive. Exercise the original writer fixtures. Preserve internal/spool/spool_test.go's legacy behavior.

Serialize each recording independently so one join/delivery cannot hold a lock needed by another's piece writes. The host supplies capture finality. Operate on explicitly supplied recordings; do not scan or migrate legacy app directories yet. Include SPEC.md and README.md in the concrete plan, describing the tested caller with app adoption pending. Run captured format, vet, build and test checks. Leave internal/mac, cmd/onair/main_darwin.go and the live tap unchanged.

issues.title: Persist recording sessions and coordinate their durable finishing
issues.body:
Build a durable session driver in new internal/recorder files using the merged pieces caller and github.com/gitdek/onair/core/session/session v0.1.0. Complete and test orchestration behind an internal interface; switch App in the next change. Only core transitions decide acceptance, Stops, capture finality, finishing order, results and end acknowledgements. Do not add another state machine or change cores, dependencies, explorers, models or trusted configuration. Injectable capture/display/finish boundaries must require no new recorder.Edge method.

Use session.New(65536, 0): IDs start at 1 in start order, never reused after acknowledgement. Persist the next identity; refuse exhaustion with an explanation. Store session.json in the spool with nonabsent records, active FIFO, parameters and necessary caller data: ID-to-directory and capture selection, reason handles with exact text, and pending end words/location. Persist whole logical state by hidden write, flush, rename and directory flush before requests or menu effects. Restore sparse state into full-capacity arrays. Release acknowledged metadata when no longer needed, retaining the identity counter.

Drive Start/RefuseStart, Stop, capture reports, RequestStop, ResumeOrClose, RequestFinish, FinishReported, RequestEndNotice and MenuSaid, including the core's scheduling obligations. Accept Start whenever capture is no longer running, even during earlier finishing. Save Stop during startup and stop immediately after successful startup. Automatic stops retain their reason. Preflight cancellation before capture was invoked ends the accepted session without invoking capture. Match asynchronous work to the current request and launch/attempt ownership. With restart limit 0, unexpected capture end or launch closes the recording for finishing without restarting capture.

Finish only as the core dispatches: one at a time, in order of permanent capture end. Drive pieces through join and delivery for each attempt. Report Handed on success, warning with each omitted piece and gap duration; report Kept with error and spool location for failed/stopped join or hand-over. Empty recordings are Kept with NothingRecordedCode and the core's exact closure cause, rendered as nothing recorded plus why. Persist results and full text before exposing the end. Display before MenuSaid, then save acknowledgement; restore unacknowledged ends with identical words and never recreate acknowledged session ends. Later successful retries of kept recordings emit separate hand-over notices, not revised or second session ends.

If a step changes session and pieces, persist session first, then pieces, before effects. On launch, with old capture dead, read all three records before effects, restore session offline and Launch it, then reconcile pieces to the recovered session and named files before dispatch. Also find recordings already absent from session whose pieces need retry or retention. Provide an import boundary for legacy recordings without inventing core state. A kill after session creation but before pieces creation must preserve the accepted recording. Pieces Recover runs once per launch, never twice through separate callers.

Keep copying and media scanning off the control path and outside app/session locks. New capture's pieces and Stop must progress while earlier finishing is blocked. Quit saves Stop and drains accepted recordings through finishing and end display before allowing edge Quit; a terminal kept error is an end too. A stopped hand-over returns a kept result instead of holding the FIFO forever. Failures waiting for launch or explicit retry must not busy-loop.

Use internal/recorder/recorder_test.go's fake-edge approach, real folders, valid boxed media and a controlled clock. Test refusal during starting/live/stopping; Start and piece writes during blocked finishing; FIFO order; startup Stop and preflight cancellation; automatic stops; no restart after failure/launch; all end outcomes including empty and gaps; saved unshown ends and acknowledgements; monotonic IDs/exhaustion; and compact serialization rather than full-capacity arrays.

Fault before/after every session and pieces save and between records, then resume fresh drivers over the same files. Include delivery success durable before outer records and delivery save-point snapshots from its existing fault tests. Check no lost accepted recording, extra capture, second joined/archive file, forgotten end or replay after acknowledgement. Test failed saves withholding unsaved effects. Keep internal/delivery/delivery_test.go's kill-at-every-step coverage intact. The final App integration will exercise the same boundaries through App itself.

Keep current App and tests working while adding this directly exercised driver. Include SPEC.md and README.md in the concrete plan: durable orchestration exists, app adoption remains pending. Run captured format, vet, build and test checks. Leave macOS files, Edge signatures, self-test spool APIs, internal/delivery implementation and live-side behavior unchanged.

issues.title: Route the recorder through the cores and recover existing spools
issues.body:
Complete issue #26 by connecting internal/recorder.App to the merged durable session and pieces callers. Replace handwritten lifecycle, finishing queue, recovery and piece-number decisions with their cores' requests. Keep internal/delivery and handover v0.1.0 unchanged. Use the established capacities, restart limit 0, millisecond durations, interruption limit 3, compact records and session-before-pieces ordering. No new model, proof, dependency or trusted configuration changes.

Refuse Start while capture runs with today's notice; accept it once capture ends permanently, even during earlier finishing. Preserve ordinary date/time names and durable identity-to-directory mappings; keep one stable joined target across retries and recovery. Latch Stop during startup and act immediately after Started. Stop or Quit during microphone permission ends the accepted recording without invoking capture; late answers start nothing. WindowClosed, failed piece writes and reaching 21,600 pieces stop through session with their reason. Unexpected capture end or launch finishes existing pieces without restarting. Quit drains finishing and end notices even when capture is already idle.

Keep capture selection, display/area/window fallback, microphone permission, microphone-start fallback, silence warnings, dropped-frame/sound reports and the live tap's forwarding behavior. Startup fallback is still preparation of the same capture request, not a session restart, and must not start again after a latched Stop. Project the active capture into the recording dot and Choices.Open; a finishing recording must not turn a newer active recording's dot grey or overwrite its capture context. Preserve current menu wording wherever the facts have not changed. Ends now say nothing recorded plus its cause for empty sessions; successful joins with omissions say how long each gap is; failed/stopped finishes say why and where their pieces are. Use the driver's durable end text and acknowledge only after display. Once acknowledged, a session end is not replayed on later launches. A subsequent successful retry says it was handed over without ending that session again.

Add an appended recorder action named RetryFailed and a Choices.CanRetry bool. The action requests another attempt for every recording whose join or hand-over failed or stopped, without affecting current capture; the field reflects whether such work exists. The menu item itself belongs to #27 and is not added here. Launch retries failed joins and failed/unresolved hand-overs. Picking a folder retries or resumes hand-overs as today, with an in-flight attempt still using its saved destination. Tidy and launch drive eligible piece retention alongside existing joined-copy cleanup: pieces go only after a confirmed hand-over and three full days from the delivery record's timestamp, at launch or within the existing hourly tick. Retry failed removals. Never remove undelivered pieces or modify unrelated files in the destination.

Migrate the existing spool without losing or duplicating recordings, including kills during migration. Identify formats from saved records and legacy done markers, not merely from a directory being present. A recording already joined by the old app carries on its saved hand-over and joined-copy retention as before and keeps its pieces; it must not be newly enrolled for piece deletion. A recording joined before hand-overs existed, with its legacy done marker and no handover.json, is left as it is. An unjoined legacy recording is imported through session and pieces core transitions, using named files as the authoritative inventory without rewriting their bytes, finished as cut short, joined and handed over once at the first launch. Save import identity and progress in the same session-before-pieces order so a repeated launch resumes the same import. Include old recordings with a prepared handover.json and a named joined file but no done marker: adopt that stable target and continue the hand-over rather than publish a second recovered name. Clean an open hidden piece remnant before other work on that recording. Preserve the core's gap manifest across a kill after join publication. Keep code retained solely to recognize legacy recordings clearly marked as such.

Load all three records and reconcile before effects. With fresh Apps over the same folders, test kills at every session, pieces and hand-over save point and between records, including imports, publication, delivery before outer success saves, end display/acknowledgement and retention. Reuse the preceding fault harness and delivery save-point fixtures, adding test support without changing delivery production behavior. Verify no lost recording, duplicate capture or joined/archive file, forgotten end or replay after acknowledgement. Test new capture writing and stopping while earlier join/delivery is blocked, with FIFO finishing. Stop still returns promptly and capture closes in about a second regardless of earlier recording size.

Before naming files for the concrete plan, include the existing behavior tests that need adaptation: internal/recorder/recorder_test.go, choice_test.go and handover_test.go, and internal/live/isolation_test.go. Their shared recorder fixture, direct Segment calls, legacy-recovery setup and joined-byte assertions use OPEN| and other strings; use valid MP4 boxes instead for everything passed through the new recorder join. Update waits that assume App.state or handing owns the lifecycle, and spool-directory assertions that formerly assumed no root session record. In recorder_test.go, TestAKilledRecordingIsRecoveredAtTheNextLaunch must require hidden-remnant removal; TestAFailedJoinLeavesThePieces and TestEveryRecoveryIsSaid must induce an actual join failure rather than expect a foreign piece to fail a partially readable recording. In handover_test.go, TestOnAirsOwnCopyGoesThreeDaysAfterTheHandOver now also expects eligible new-recording pieces to go, while explicit old-format recordings keep them. Empty-start and microphone-cancellation tests must allow the durable session ledger and require the new nothing-recorded end semantics. Preserve the assertions for target fallback and microphone behavior, and TestTheRecorderIsTheSameWhateverTheLiveSideDoes must still compare all edge calls and files with and without the live side after its media fixture is converted. Review internal/recorder/live_test.go, internal/spool/spool_test.go and internal/delivery/delivery_test.go as preservation constraints; name them only if an existing test actually needs an edit. Add real-writer end-to-end tests that deliver all six original fixture pieces with no omissions.

Keep internal/mac and cmd/onair/main_darwin.go untouched. Every exported name they use retains its signature: recorder.New, Config, Choices, Display, Area, Local, existing actions and events, and App.Menu, Event, Segment, Launched, Tidy, FolderChosen, Displays, PickDisplay, AreaPicked and WindowPicked. Add no Edge method and preserve existing enum values. Preserve spool.Create, Recording, PutOpening, PutPiece, Pieces and Join, including the core-free self-test behavior. The live tap and selection settings remain compatible.

Include SPEC.md and README.md in the concrete plan and update actual recorder behavior, the session/pieces callers, persistence, retries, retention, rules 1/2/3/4/9 and milestone status. Distinguish completed Linux tests from unperformed Mac checks; docs/PRD.md's intended rules are not weakened or marked hand-checked. Run the captured format, vet, build and test checks.

Merger work for a person: after checks and merge, BEFORE rebuilding the owner's running app from main, run go test ./..., onair selftest and a short recording delivered whole with no omitted piece on the Mac; CI cannot compile that side. Run PRD checks 3 and 4 through the cores: kill/power loss recovers and delivers at launch without continuing capture. Repeat check 1 for changed piece writes. Record actual results. Checks 6/7 await #27, check 2 awaits #28 and check 5 awaits #29. Unavailable Docker/network checks are a handoff, not scope expansion.

Out of scope: the retry menu item (#27), capture restart (#28), disk guard core/caller (#10/#29), the hand-over v0.2.0 upgrade and #16, two-/four-hour prompts, keyboard shortcut, rule 12's network test and excluding a second On Air process from the spool. All work needed for #26 itself is completed here and in the three preceding changes.

usage.summary: Wrote [issues.json](issues.json) with four ordered plumbing changes covering media handling, durable core callers, and app integration with migration. The plan checker passed on the first check; `repo/` is unchanged.
